context:
Start with the result contract and tests, then wire producers. Do not try to
infer Docker or cloud shape from platform name alone; record source and
collection status for every normalized field. Reuse the existing
`platform_info` output and `platform_config_utils` helpers where possible,
but treat them as inputs to a normalized contract rather than the contract
itself. Add Docker inspection as an optional metadata collection step outside
measured benchmark timing. For cloud platforms, prefer observed metadata when
permissions allow and fall back to sanitized requested config with
`source="requested"` when observation is unavailable.
description:
Benchmark results currently capture the client host environment and a
platform-specific `platform_info` block, but they do not fully describe where
the measured database engine actually ran. This is misleading for common local
development and integration-test workflows where BenchBox runs on macOS while
the data platform runs in a Linux Docker container because the platform is not
natively compatible with macOS.

The same gap exists for cloud runs. Some adapters capture useful fields such
as region, warehouse size, workgroup, storage bucket, reservation, or cluster
metadata, but those fields are adapter-specific and exported as raw config
rather than a stable result contract. Downstream consumers cannot reliably
compare or filter benchmark results by runtime type, container image, cloud
provider, region, compute shape, storage configuration, or whether a field was
requested by the user vs observed from the platform.

Build a normalized execution-environment contract for result artifacts that
separates:
  - the BenchBox client process host;
  - the measured platform runtime;
  - requested platform options;
  - observed platform deployment details;
  - cloud provider, region, compute, and storage facets;
  - raw adapter metadata retained for compatibility; and
  - anonymized/redacted public export behavior.

anti_patterns.dont: add Docker inspection to measured query execution timing
anti_patterns.instead: collect before/after measured phases and record collection status.
anti_patterns.why: environment capture must not perturb benchmark timings

anti_patterns.dont: fail a benchmark because cloud metadata APIs lack permission
anti_patterns.instead: record unavailable metadata with the error class and continue.
anti_patterns.why: benchmark execution can still be valid

anti_patterns.dont: flatten cloud region, compute, and storage into adapter-specific `platform.config` only
anti_patterns.why: downstream consumers need stable cross-platform facets

anti_patterns.dont: make every adapter implement a new required abstract method in one migration
anti_patterns.instead: add optional hooks and conservative defaults.
anti_patterns.why: that creates a risky broad adapter change

anti_patterns.instead: sanitize, classify, and apply anonymization before export.
anti_patterns.why: they can contain credentials and infrastructure identifiers

anti_patterns.dont: represent localhost server adapters as native local database processes
anti_patterns.instead: use `unknown` until Docker or explicit runtime metadata proves the substrate.
anti_patterns.why: many localhost services are Docker-backed Linux runtimes on macOS

preserves.behavior: Anonymized exports never include raw passwords, tokens, private keys, access keys, credential file paths, or full connection strings.
Benchmarks do not fail when Docker, cloud metadata APIs, or permissioned system introspection are unavailable; results must record unavailable metadata explicitly.
Existing `platform_info`, `platform.config`, `system_profile`, `driver_metadata`, and `engine_version` consumers keep receiving equivalent data during the migration.
Existing cloud adapters remain lazy about optional SDK imports and do not require cloud credentials during unit tests.
Existing result JSON artifacts without normalized environment fields continue to load and export through the compatibility path.
No benchmark timing path includes Docker or cloud metadata collection in the measured query execution duration.

work_units.notes:
Add explicit result-model fields for:
  - `environment.client_host`: current `system_profile` shape, kept for
    backward compatibility with existing host metadata.
  - `environment.platform_runtime`: runtime type
    (`local_process`, `docker_container`, `remote_server`,
    `managed_cloud`, `serverless`, `dataframe_process`, `unknown`),
    OS, arch, engine process host when known, and collection status.
  - `environment.container`: Docker engine/version, image, image digest,
    container id/name, container OS/arch, requested platform, CPU limit,
    memory limit, port mappings, relevant bind mounts/volumes, and
    collection errors. This block must be absent or explicitly
    `collection_status="unavailable"` when Docker is not involved.
  - `platform.deployment`: deployment type, connection mode, service
    endpoint class (`localhost_port`, `remote_host`, `cloud_endpoint`,
    `embedded_process`), and whether runtime metadata was requested,
    observed, inferred, or unavailable.
  - `platform.cloud`: provider, region/location, account/project/workspace
    identifiers after anonymization policy is applied.
  - `platform.compute`: warehouse, cluster, serverless slots, RPU, node
    type/count, worker/driver shape, cache/result-cache flags, and source.
  - `platform.storage`: data table format, staging location, bucket/prefix,
    storage tier, compression, cleanup policy, and source.
  - `platform.raw_config` and `platform.raw_metadata`: existing
    adapter-specific output retained for compatibility and diagnostics.
Keep the current top-level `environment` and `platform.config` keys
readable by old consumers during the transition, but make the normalized
fields the canonical contract in tests and docs.
work_units.summary: Define the normalized execution-environment result contract

work_units.notes:
Map Databricks requested config and SDK-observed warehouse metadata into
the new contract: workspace host, catalog/schema/http path, warehouse
id/name/size/type, serverless flag, photon flag, min/max clusters, spot
policy, runtime/channel, and state. Add an explicit region field when it
can be configured or observed; otherwise record
`collection_status="unavailable"`. Add fixture-backed tests without live
Databricks credentials.

Map ClickHouse Cloud requested config and any observed service metadata
into the new contract: managed deployment, auth mode, service endpoint,
staging URL type, and region/compute fields when exposed by config or API
metadata. Add fixture-backed tests for fully populated and sparse metadata
cases.

Map Firebolt requested config and observed metadata into the new contract:
account/engine/database identifiers, endpoint class, deployment mode,
engine shape when available, and explicit missing-region status when the
region cannot be observed. Add fixture-backed tests for core and cloud
deployment modes.

Current export anonymization focuses on host environment. Extend it to
every field that can reveal infrastructure identity:
  - hostnames, account ids, project ids, workspace urls, http paths,
    bucket names, prefixes, database/schema names, warehouse names,
    workgroup names, cluster ids, IAM role ARNs, container names, bind
    mount paths, and usernames;
  - secret-like keys such as password, token, secret, access_key,
    private_key, session token, connection string, and credential file.
Public export should hash stable identifiers when comparisons need
grouping and redact values when grouping is not needed. Private/internal
result export can preserve raw metadata only behind an explicit option.
Add tests that prove no raw secrets or obvious infrastructure identifiers
remain after anonymized JSON export.
work_units.summary: Extend anonymization and redaction across platform, config, and execution metadata
Add result-schema compatibility tests and golden fixtures

work_units.notes:
Update development and result-artifact docs with the canonical field
meanings, source/provenance rules, anonymization policy, and examples for
local process, Docker-backed local server, remote self-hosted server,
managed cloud warehouse, and serverless cloud. Include a migration note
for existing `platform.config`, `system_profile`, and `platform_metadata`

work_units.summary: Document the environment-capture contract and migration guidance

work_units.notes:
The CLI already parses `--platform-option` and uses those values to build
`DatabaseConfig`, but the standard lifecycle does not reliably persist
them into `execution_metadata.run_config.platform_options`.
Update the run/orchestration path so result artifacts include sanitized
requested platform options with source provenance:
  - registered default;
  - saved credential/config;
  - environment variable;
  - CLI option;
  - runtime override.
Preserve enough detail to reconstruct region, warehouse/instance shape,
storage bucket/prefix, table format, deployment mode, and local Docker
service hints. Do not persist raw secrets; secret-like keys must be
redacted before reaching result export.
work_units.summary: Propagate requested platform options into result metadata with provenance

work_units.notes:
Touch `BenchmarkResults`, `ResultBuilder`, `result_factory`, and
`schema.build_result_payload` so the result object carries both the
BenchBox process host profile and the measured platform runtime profile.
Existing `system_profile` input should continue to work and populate
`environment.client_host`. New normalized runtime/deployment fields should
be generated by the builder even when adapters only provide legacy
`platform_info`, using conservative `unknown`/`unavailable` statuses
rather than guesses.
work_units.summary: Refactor result builder/exporter to emit client host vs platform runtime

work_units.notes:
Add a small Docker metadata collector that is optional, best-effort, and
unit-testable without a live daemon. It should discover BenchBox-managed
or known integration-test containers by compose labels, service name,
image name, exposed host port, and adapter config. Capture image tag and
digest, container platform, OS/arch, CPU/memory limits, port mappings,
bind mounts/volumes, container state, Docker engine version when
available, and collection errors. When Docker is absent, unavailable, or
permission-denied, the result must say so explicitly without failing the
benchmark.
Cover ClickHouse Server, Trino, Presto, PostgreSQL, StarRocks, Doris,
SingleStore, Databend, and other Docker integration platforms that connect
through localhost ports.
work_units.summary: Add Docker runtime discovery for local container-backed platforms

work_units.notes:
Add base-platform helpers so adapters can return normalized metadata
without duplicating schema assembly. The default path should map existing
`get_platform_info()` output into conservative normalized fields:
  - embedded engines and DataFrame adapters become local process or
    dataframe process runtimes;
  - localhost server adapters remain `unknown` until Docker discovery or
    explicit runtime metadata proves containerization;
  - remote host adapters become `remote_server`;
  - cloud adapters become `managed_cloud` or `serverless`.
Avoid making every adapter implement a new required abstract method in
one PR. Add optional hooks/mixins and migrate adapters incrementally.
work_units.summary: Add base adapter hooks for normalized runtime and deployment metadata

work_units.notes:
Map existing Snowflake requested config and observed metadata into the
new contract: cloud provider, region, account, role, database/schema,
warehouse name/size/type, min/max clusters, auto suspend/resume, query
acceleration, scaling policy, and result cache. Add fixture-backed unit
tests that cover both successful warehouse metadata collection and
permission-denied/unavailable metadata without live Snowflake credentials.

Map existing BigQuery requested config and observed metadata into the new
contract: provider, project, dataset, location, storage bucket/prefix,
job priority/cache settings, reservation assignment, slot capacity, and
pricing/reservation model when available. Add fixture-backed unit tests
that cover on-demand, reservation-backed, and metadata-unavailable cases
without live BigQuery credentials.

Map existing Redshift requested config and observed metadata into the new
contract: AWS region, serverless vs provisioned deployment,
namespace/workgroup or cluster id, RPU or node type/count, storage
capacity when available, S3 staging bucket/prefix, IAM role presence, and
result cache. Add fixture-backed tests for both serverless and
provisioned metadata shapes without live AWS credentials.

Map Athena requested config into the new serverless contract: AWS
provider, region, workgroup, catalog/database, S3 output location,
staging root, data format, compression, cleanup policy, and serverless
runtime type. Add fixture-backed tests that prove missing optional fields
are represented as unavailable, not silently omitted.
